What it does, in order Preflight. Python 3.11+, systemd, and a hermes binary it can find. It stops with a clear message rather than half-installing. Service account. Unpairing and revocation Removing a device in the app deletes its key. Revoking from the host closes that device's link immediately and refuses the next connection — the token it held is spent. Neither touches your bots, your profiles or anything else on the host.

How it works The Mac app is the executor . Your host sends a command; the app performs it under your account and returns the result. The Mac dials out and keeps the socket open, so nothing listens on it and Remote Login stays off. It starts switched off. Nothing is queried until you turn on Settings → Computer → Let bo

From a bot's shell hermey computer observe hermey computer act '[{"kind":"click","x":120,"y":80}]' Copy The same commands are documented for agents in the shared mac-local-computer skill that the bridge installs for every bot on the host.

Runbook Confirm this is the right host. Hermes must already run here and have profiles the human talks to. Hard rules Never bind the bridge to anything but 127.0.0.1 . tailscale serve is the only front door. Never create a unit named hermes-gateway.service . That is Hermes' messaging gateway. Never add App Transport Security exceptions to the apps. The certificate must be real. Never stop or reconfigure an existing tailnet

No tailnet Install with --no-serve , terminate TLS in front of 127.0.0.1:8787 with a real certificate, and give the apps that URL. Self-signed certificates are refused — do not work around that in the app.
Start here hermey doctor Copy It reports the unit state, loopback health, the gateway URL the bridge relays to, Tailscale's state, and whether the HTTPS endpoint answers through the certificate.

Doctor says health FAIL The bridge is not answering on 127.0.0.1:8787 . Read its log; the first line usually names the cause. hermey logs 80 Copy Log line Meaning address already in use something else holds the port — sudo ss -ltnp | grep 8787 , then reinstall with --port 8788 "event": "upstream_error" with "reason": "

"Reusing this host's dashboard: pid …" Expected. Hermes allows one dashboard per host and the installer reuses it. For a second isolated one while testing, use HERMEY_UNIT_PREFIX and a separate HERMEY_CONF , and point the second bridge at a dashboard you started with --isolated .
tailscale serve refused tailscale status tailscale serve status Copy If another service owns 8443 , re-run the installer with --https-port 8444 . Do not stop the other service to make room.

h: HTTPS fails but the bridge is healthy
b: HTTPS fails but the bridge is healthy Tailscale issues the certificate on first use; a fresh domain can take a minute. If it persists: tailscale cert <host>.<tailnet>.ts.net curl -v https://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net:8443/v1/health Copy

h: The app cannot reach the host
b: The app cannot reach the host Is the device on the tailnet, logged into the same one? Does the URL in the app exactly match hermey pair 's output, including the port? curl https://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net:8443/v1/health from another tailnet device — if that fails, the problem is the host, not the app.
A pairing code is rejected Codes are single-use and expire in minutes. Mint a fresh one with hermey pair . Repeated failures are rate limited per client, so wait a moment after a handful of attempts.

h: The iOS app stops launching after a week
b: The iOS app stops launching after a week That is free-Apple-ID signing, not a bug. Re-sign through AltStore or SideStore, or use a paid developer account for a one-year profile.

h: macOS says the app is damaged
b: macOS says the app is damaged The build is unsigned. Right-click → Open the first time, or once: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Hermey.app Copy

Computer use keeps dropping The Mac app must be running to hold the link. A machine that sleeps loses its socket; the app re-verifies on wake, and the host drops a Mac that stops answering so callers fail fast instead of hanging. The feed and the download are published separately, and GitHub Pages serves the feed before the disk image it points at, so a check in that window finds a version whose file is still 404 . No

Trust boundaries Boundary Crossing it requires What is on the other side Public internet → tailnet Tailscale identity + ACL nothing: no public ingress exists Tailnet → bridge TLS to tailscale serve , then a single-use 30 s ticket pairing, tokens, /v1/ws Bridge → gateway loopback plus the gateway token, which is never s

Invariants The bridge listens on loopback only; tailscale serve is the only front door. Tickets are single-use and expire in 30 seconds; a device is identified by its own Ed25519 key. The device never receives the gateway token — it cannot talk to the agent directly. Approvals are the agent's to ask and the human's to

Deliberately absent No account, no analytics, no crash reporting, no relay of ours in the request path. No public ingress: if the tailnet is up but the device is not on it, nothing is reachable. No per-bot permission system on the Mac. Computer use is one owner-level switch — a small number of trusted bots is the state

Where the apps keep secrets The phone keeps its device key and refresh token in the Keychain, this-device-only. The Mac build ships unsigned and has no Keychain entitlement, so it keeps the same items in a 0600 file under ~/Library/Application Support/Hermey/ , excluded from backups.

Reporting a problem Open a private advisory at https://github.com/macblizzard/hermey/security/advisories/new rather than a public issue, and do not paste tokens, hostnames or personal data into either.
